headline: Mariana has lost 8% of her body weight (77.9 to 71.7 kg) from Sep 5 to Nov 24, 2026, with poor appetite. Her son and primary caregiver also reports exhaustion and has asked for respite.

items.statement: Weight fell from 77.9 kg (Sep 5) to 75.7 kg (Oct 1), 73.6 kg (Oct 28) and 71.7 kg (Nov 24). That is a 6.2 kg (13.7 lb), 8.0% loss over about 11 weeks, with a steady decline at each reading.
items.verifier_note: The four weights match the vitals record. The change of -6.2 kg, -13.7 lb and -8.0% matches. Sep 5 to Nov 24 is about 11 weeks, and each reading is lower than the one before.

items.statement: On Nov 24 the dietitian documented poor appetite, skipped breakfasts, and eating about 50% of day center lunches. The plan is an oral nutrition supplement twice daily, weekly weights, and a dental check for chewing problems.
items.verifier_note: The Nov 24 dietitian note states the appetite, breakfast and lunch findings and the plan exactly as the statement does.

items.statement: On Sep 27 the social worker met with Marcus, her son and primary caregiver. He reported exhaustion and poor sleep, said he is worried about managing evenings alone, and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed. No follow-up outcome appears in the notes.
items.verifier_note: The Sep 27 social work note matches every detail. It does not record an outcome, so the statement that no follow-up appears is consistent with it.

items.statement: The PCP notes of Sep 2, Sep 27 and Nov 27 say chronic conditions are stable with the current plan continued. The Nov 27 note does not mention the weight loss documented on Nov 24.
items.verifier_note: All three PCP notes say conditions are stable and the plan continues. The Nov 27 note does not mention the weight loss documented in the Nov 24 dietitian note.

items.statement: Some earlier notes report Mariana in good spirits and engaged in day center activities. Her day center attendance was documented on Oct 9, and she joined the gardening group on Oct 4. Blood pressure readings (130/74, 134/77, 130/72) stayed below the 140/90 threshold. There were no medication changes and no encounters in the period.
items.verifier_note: The Sep 21 and Oct 26 notes say good spirits. The Oct 9 and Oct 4 notes match the day center attendance and gardening group. The BP values are all below 140/90. The medication and encounter records are empty.

questions_for_team: Is the dietitian's plan (supplement twice daily, weekly weights, dental check) in place, and who is following it up?
Should the PCP review the 8% weight loss, given the Nov 27 note records no concern?
Has respite been arranged for Marcus since Sep 27, and what support is there for evenings?
Is there a way to improve intake at day center lunches, which are about 50% eaten, and to address skipped breakfasts at home?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters, ED visits, and admissions in that window, noting reason and discharge follow-up, given ischemic heart disease and CKD stage 1 with diabetes.
Falls and near-falls check: any falls, fall-related injuries, or new fall-risk concerns, given age 81 and osteoporosis (fracture risk).

Medication changes since last review: starts, stops, and dose changes across the active list (metoprolol succinate, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin 20 mg, vitamin B12 injections). Check for any new antihypertensive, antidiabetic, or antiplatelet/anticoagulant agents that are not on the active list, and confirm reconciliation against pharmacy fill records.
Nitroglycerin use: frequency of PRN use or chest-pain episodes reported in the window, since this may signal ischemic heart disease instability and warrants team discussion.
Blood pressure trend across the window against the essential hypertension history, including any orthostatic readings and dizziness reports, given beta-blocker use.
Glycemic data: any HbA1c, fasting glucose, or hyperglycemia readings in the window, given type 2 diabetes, prediabetes history, and metabolic syndrome. Check whether the diabetes plan is current.
Renal function: most recent eGFR and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, given CKD stage 1 linked to diabetes; note whether labs are due in the window.

Weight and BMI trend (obesity, BMI 30+ on record), plus any appetite or intake change. Check hemoglobin and CBC given the anemia diagnosis and B12 injection schedule, and confirm B12 injections are on time.
Lipid panel and statin review: last triglyceride and LDL values, given simvastatin and hypertriglyceridemia history, and whether a lipid recheck is due.

Function, cognition, mood, and caregiver: ADL/IADL changes, any cognitive screen results, mood or attendance concerns at the program, and caregiver status or needs. Also confirm care-plan items due in the window (bone density or osteoporosis follow-up, eye and foot exams for diabetes, immunizations, advance directive review).
